entries.Title: Directive 2011/92/EU on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (codification)
entries.Authority: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
entries.Notes: Mandates EIA for pipelines >800mm diameter and >40km length (Annex I, item 16). Amended by Directive 2014/52/EU. Establishes screening, scoping, and consultation procedures for environmental assessment of development projects likely to have significant environmental effects. Requires public participation and transboundary consultation.

entries.Title: Directive 2014/52/EU amending Directive 2011/92/EU on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment
entries.Authority: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
entries.Notes: Amends Directive 2011/92/EU to strengthen environmental assessment procedures. Introduces requirement for consideration of human health, reasonable alternatives, and enhanced public participation. Member States transposition deadline was 16 May 2017.

entries.Title: Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council establishing a framework for Community action in the field of water policy (Water Framework Directive)
entries.Authority: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
entries.Notes: Establishes framework for protection of surface waters, groundwater, and protection of groundwater-dependent terrestrial ecosystems (GWDTE). Requires achievement of 'good status' by 2027. Prohibits significant damage to GWDTE and sets quantitative/chemical quality objectives. River basin management plans required.

entries.Title: Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora (Habitats Directive)
entries.Authority: Council of the European Union
entries.Notes: Establishes Natura 2000 network of Special Areas of Conservation (SACs) and designates protected habitat types and species. Article 6 Appropriate Assessment required for projects potentially affecting Natura 2000 sites. Requires assessment of mitigation for adverse effects on conservation objectives.

entries.Title: Regulation (EU) 2022/869 on guidelines for trans-European energy infrastructure (TEN-E Regulation)
entries.Authority: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
entries.Notes: Revised framework for trans-European energy infrastructure. CRITICAL: Oil and gas pipelines NO LONGER eligible for Projects of Common Interest (PCI) status as of 2022 revision. Focus shifted to renewable gases, hydrogen, and electrification. Identifies 11 priority corridors aligned with EU Green Deal climate objectives.

entries.Title: Directive 2012/18/EU on the control of major-accident hazards involving dangerous substances (Seveso III Directive)
entries.Authority: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
entries.Notes: Controls major accident hazards at industrial establishments. Excludes transport pipelines but may apply to pumping stations and fixed bulk storage. Requires Major Accident Prevention Policy (MAPP), Safety Reports, and land-use planning. Pipeline companies transporting hazardous substances should verify applicability to storage/pumping facilities.

entries.Title: 49 CFR Part 192 - Transportation of Natural and Other Gas by Pipeline: Minimum Federal Safety Standards
entries.Authority: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), U.S. Department of Transportation
entries.Notes: Establishes minimum federal safety standards for natural gas pipelines. Covers design, construction, testing, operation, and maintenance. Specifies materials, pressure limits, welding standards, inspection intervals, and integrity management programs. Non-retroactive for pre-1971 pipelines. Applies to all natural gas pipelines in USA.

entries.Title: 49 CFR Part 195 - Transportation of Hazardous Liquids by Pipeline
entries.Authority: Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), U.S. Department of Transportation
entries.Notes: Establishes minimum federal safety standards for hazardous liquid pipelines (petroleum, petroleum products, anhydrous ammonia, other hazardous substances). Similar framework to Part 192 but tailored for liquid transport. Includes design, construction, testing, operation, integrity management, and emergency response requirements.

entries.Title: National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA)
entries.Authority: U.S. Congress; implemented by federal agencies
entries.Notes: Procedural statute requiring federal agencies to prepare Environmental Impact Statements (EIS) or Environmental Assessments (EA) for major federal actions. FERC is lead agency for interstate gas pipelines. Recent Supreme Court decision (Seven County Infrastructure Coalition v. Eagle County, May 2025) narrows scope of indirect/cumulative impacts analysis. Accelerates permitting timelines.

entries.Title: Natural Gas Act, Section 7 - Certification of interstate natural gas pipelines
entries.Authority: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), pursuant to 15 U.S.C. §717f
entries.Notes: Authorizes FERC to issue Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) for interstate natural gas pipelines and LNG facilities. Standard: 'public convenience and necessity.' FERC acts as lead federal agency for NEPA coordination. FERC Policy Statement (PL18-1-000, 2018) outlines certification process. Amended multiple times; current version reflects Energy Policy Act 2005.

entries.Title: Clean Water Act, Section 404 - Permits for discharge of dredged or fill material
entries.Authority: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), pursuant to 33 U.S.C. §1344
entries.Notes: Requires USACE permit for discharge of dredged or fill material into waters of the US (WOTUS), including wetlands. Pipeline crossings typically authorized under individual permits or Nationwide Permit 12 (NWP 12). EPA has authority to veto permits. Section 401 requires state water quality certification. 404(b)(1) Guidelines compliance mandatory.

entries.Title: Clean Water Act, Section 401 - Water Quality Certification
entries.Authority: States and Indian Tribes, under delegation from EPA, pursuant to 33 U.S.C. §1341
entries.Notes: Requires certification from state or tribe that federal permit activity will comply with state water quality standards. States may grant, condition, or deny certification. Certificate required before USACE can issue 404 permit or FERC can issue pipeline certificate. Applies to all pipeline crossings of state waters.

entries.Title: Endangered Species Act, Section 7 - Interagency consultation
entries.Authority: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service (USFWS) and National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Fisheries, pursuant to 16 U.S.C. §1536
entries.Notes: Requires federal action agencies to consult with USFWS/NOAA Fisheries if project may affect listed threatened/endangered species or critical habitat. Two-track process: Informal (NLAA + concurrence) or Formal (90-day consultation + Biological Opinion within 135 days). Incidental Take Statement issued with BO. Section 7 consultation often most time-intensive permitting step.

entries.Title: National Historic Preservation Act, Section 106 - Historic property review
entries.Authority: Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP), State Historic Preservation Officers (SHPOs), Tribal Historic Preservation Officers (THPOs)
entries.Notes: Requires federal agencies to consider effects of undertakings on historic properties (listed in or eligible for National Register). Four-step process: Initiation → Identify Historic Properties → Assess Effects → Resolve Adverse Effects. Consultation with SHPOs, THPOs, ACHP. Memoranda of Agreement (MOA) document mitigation. Applies to FERC certificates and Army Corps permits.

entries.Title: California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
entries.Authority: State of California, CPUC, Coastal Commission, Regional Water Quality Control Boards
entries.Notes: California state environmental review law. Requires lead agencies to prepare Environmental Impact Reports (EIRs) or Negative Declarations for projects with potential environmental impacts. CPUC has authority for intrastate gas pipeline siting. Coastal Commission has jurisdiction in coastal zone. State water boards regulate discharges. Much stricter than federal NEPA; litigation-prone.

entries.Title: Texas Administrative Code, Title 16, Part 3 - Pipeline Safety Rules (adopted by Railroad Commission of Texas)
entries.Authority: Railroad Commission of Texas (RRC)
entries.Notes: Texas state pipeline safety regulations for intrastate pipelines. Incorporates 49 CFR Parts 192/195 by reference with state-specific additions. Group A pipelines (transmission/gathering) require T-4 Permit to Operate. RRC has jurisdiction over ~1/6 of US pipeline infrastructure. Interstate lines fall under federal PHMSA jurisdiction.

entries.Title: Canadian Energy Regulator Act (S.C. 2019, c. 28, s. 10)
entries.Authority: Canada Energy Regulator (CER), federal independent agency
entries.SourceTitle: Justice Laws Website: Canadian Energy Regulator Act
entries.Notes: Federal law establishing Canada Energy Regulator (successor to NEB). Regulates ~100 companies operating ~73,000 km of interprovincial/international pipelines. Requires safety management, environmental protection, emergency response, integrity management, and third-party crossing programs. CER has compliance authority including AMPs up to $100k per company per infraction per day.

entries.Title: Canadian Energy Regulator Onshore Pipeline Regulations (SOR/99-294)
entries.Authority: Canada Energy Regulator
entries.SourceTitle: Justice Laws Website: Onshore Pipeline Regulations
entries.Notes: Technical regulations for federally-regulated onshore pipelines. Implements design, construction, operation, maintenance, abandonment standards. Requires CSA Z662 compliance. Section 6 establishes pipeline lifecycle requirements ensuring safety, security, environmental protection. CER Guidance Notes provide implementation clarity.

entries.Title: Impact Assessment Act (S.C. 2019, c. 22, s. 1)
entries.Authority: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (IAAC) and CER (integrated assessments)
entries.SourceTitle: Justice Laws Website: Impact Assessment Act
entries.Notes: Federal environmental assessment law. Applies to designated projects ≥75 km new right-of-way. IAAC leads assessments; CER participates in integrated assessments. Timeline: 300 days (agency-led) to 600 days (review panel). Climate change impacts analysis mandatory. Note: Designated projects provision partially struck down by Supreme Court (Alberta v. Canada, 2023) but remains operative with narrower scope.

entries.Title: National Energy Board Pipeline Crossing Regulations (SOR/88-528)
entries.Authority: Canada Energy Regulator (formerly National Energy Board)
entries.SourceTitle: Justice Laws Website: Pipeline Crossing Regulations
entries.Notes: Governs third-party crossings of federally-regulated pipelines. Requires CER leave for most crossings (exemptions for minor facilities with pipeline company permission). Specifies safe-work protocols, prior notification requirements, mechanical excavation restrictions within 3m of pipes, hand-exposure requirements. Critical for protecting pipeline integrity.

entries.Title: Pipeline Act (R.S.A. 2000, c. P-15) and Pipeline Regulation (Alberta Regulation 91/2019)
entries.Authority: Alberta Energy Regulator (AER)
entries.Notes: Alberta provincial law regulating intrastate pipelines. AER has jurisdiction over provincial pipelines. Requires design, construction, operation compliance with CSA Z662. Integrity management programs required. AER conducts risk-based inspections. Audits company management systems. Enforces compliance through orders, penalties.

entries.Title: Environmental Guidelines for the Location, Construction and Operation of Hydrocarbon Pipelines and Facilities in Ontario (7th Edition)
entries.Authority: Ontario Energy Board (OEB)
entries.Notes: Ontario regulatory guidance for transmission pipeline leave-to-construct applications. Establishes environmental review standards and consultation protocols. Ontario Pipeline Coordinating Committee (OPCC) formed for routing/siting input. Transmission pipelines require OEB application for leave to construct.

entries.Title: Federal Law No. (24) of 1999 Concerning the Protection and Development of the Environment
entries.Authority: Ministry of Climate Change and Environment (MOCCAE) and Environment Agency - Abu Dhabi (EAD)
entries.Notes: Federal environmental law establishing EIA framework for UAE. Article 3 requires identification of project categories requiring EIA. Article 4 mandates environmental licensing before construction. Projects cannot commence activities without environmental permit. Establishes monitoring requirements and waste management standards for oil/gas operations. Forms basis for all UAE environmental permitting.

entries.Title: Abu Dhabi Emirate Environment, Health and Safety Management System (EHSMS) Regulatory Framework (Decree 42 of 2009)
entries.Authority: Environment Agency - Abu Dhabi (EAD)
entries.Notes: Abu Dhabi emirate-level regulatory framework implementing federal environmental law. Establishes EIA format/content requirements including project description, baseline conditions, environmental impact assessment (magnitude/reversibility/permanence), mitigation measures, monitoring programs. Construction Environmental Management Plans (CEMPs) may be required post-EIA approval. Competent Authorities review compliance with health/safety elements.
